title: Role of composition-tuned disorder on magnetic exchange interactions in NiRuMnGa
authors: Manikantha Panda, Prabuddha Kant Mishra, Vinod Kumar, Wilfrid Prellier, Rahul Sharma, Tapas Paramanik
abstract: We report the experimental investigation of the quaternary Heusler alloy NiRuMnGa, complemented by first-principles calculations. The energetically favorable crystal structure was identified from first-principles calculations and subsequently used as the structural model for refinement of the powder X-ray diffraction data. The refinement shows good agreement with the experimental pattern and reveals substantial B2-type disorder involving Ni/Ru and Mn/Ga site intermixing. The dc magnetic response exhibits pronounced ZFC--FC irreversibility near $\sim 48$ K, with the irreversibility temperature shifting toward lower temperatures under increasing magnetic field, indicating a field-sensitive glassy state. The isothermal magnetization remains unsaturated up to 7 T, reaching only $\sim 0.4\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$/f.u., accompanied by pronounced hysteresis, suggesting competing exchange interactions and frustrated magnetic moments. AC susceptibility, together with magnetic relaxation and memory measurements, confirms slow spin dynamics characteristic of a cluster glass state. The lack of a discernible heat-capacity anomaly near the irreversibility temperature further supports the absence of conventional long-range magnetic order. Collectively, these results demonstrate that competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions in NiRuMnGa leads to magnetic frustration and stabilizes a cluster glass state.
summary: This paper experimentally and computationally investigates the magnetic properties of the NiRuMnGa Heusler alloy, focusing on the impact of compositional disorder. The findings reveal strong evidence for magnetic frustration due to competing exchange interactions, leading to a cluster glass state rather than conventional long-range magnetic order. This work highlights how structural imperfections can stabilize complex, disordered magnetic ground states.
main_problem: The study investigates how compositional disorder affects the magnetic exchange interactions within the quaternary Heusler alloy NiRuMnGa.
main_result: The competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, exacerbated by structural disorder, leads to the stabilization of a cluster glass magnetic state in the material.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (PXRD, DC/AC magnetometry, heat capacity) with first-principles electronic structure calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quaternary Heusler alloy NiRuMnGa. The structural disorder is characterized as B2-type site intermixing, and the magnetic behavior is modeled by analyzing competing exchange interactions.
key_observables: ZFC-FC irreversibility, slow spin dynamics (AC susceptibility), unsaturated magnetization, and the absence of a conventional heat-capacity anomaly.
important_parameters: The magnetic transition temperature ($\sim 48$ K), the applied magnetic field (up to 7 T), and the degree of site disorder.
main_assumptions: The study assumes the LiMgPdSn-type crystal structure and interprets the magnetic response based on established models for glassy magnetic states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, spin-resolved DOS, and magnetic measurements (ZFC/FC curves, AC susceptibility) confirming glassy magnetic behavior.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of structural characterization (PXRD/Rietveld refinement revealing disorder), electronic structure calculation (DOS/polarization), and comprehensive magnetic characterization (DC/AC measurements) to build a case for magnetic frustration.
why_interesting: The focus on glassy magnetic states, spin-glass behavior, and the role of structural disorder in mediating complex magnetic interactions is highly relevant to understanding frustrated quantum many-body systems.
